# Replay

> Replay makes software visible. The core product is Replay QA — an autonomous QA agent that takes a URL, explores a web application, records every session, finds real bugs, and returns a detailed bug report with root cause, suggested fix, and a full Replay recording. No test suite required. No QA team required.

## Product

- [Replay QA](https://qa.replay.io): Autonomous QA for web applications. Give it a URL and it explores the app like a user, writes Playwright tests, records every session with Replay's deterministic recording engine, and files detailed bug reports. Each report includes a root cause diagnosis, a specific suggested fix, and a full Replay recording with runtime evidence. Designed for AI-built apps and teams shipping fast.
- [Replay for CI](https://replay-marketing-site-v2.netlify.app/ci-agent): Replay QA integrated into CI pipelines. Records every Playwright or Cypress test run, analyzes every failure, and posts root cause and fix to the PR automatically.
- [Replay QA API](mailto:sales@replay.io): REST API for embedding Replay QA as a quality gate in software factories and AI coding platforms. Every app generated by the system gets automatically tested before it ships.

## How It Works

1. **Give it a URL** — point Replay QA at any web app. No configuration, no test files.
2. **Autonomous exploration** — Replay QA navigates the app the way a user would, discovers meaningful user journeys, and writes Playwright tests for each one.
3. **Replay recording** — every test run is executed in a Replay-instrumented browser. The full runtime is captured deterministically: every function call, DOM mutation, network request, and state change.
4. **Bug report** — for every bug found, Replay QA files a report with root cause, a suggested fix, confidence score, and a link to the Replay recording. The report is designed to be consumed directly by a coding agent.

## Agent Integration

Replay QA exposes a REST API at `https://loop-qa.replay.io/api/v1`. The OpenAPI spec is at `/api/v1/openapi.json`. Agents can use this prompt to set up a continuous QA loop:

> Use Replay QA to test this app. Create a QA project for my running app, wait for the results, fix any open bugs, and keep looping until the app passes.

Full agent prompt: create a QA project with `target_url`, poll status until complete, read each open bug's root-caused report, apply the fix, mark it fixed via the API, and loop until no open bugs remain. Supports localhost apps via reverse proxy.

## Issue Tracker Integration

Replay QA supports a Bug Report Webhook. Configure an endpoint URL and Replay QA will POST each bug report as JSON with `body` (bug description), `referrer`, and a `callback_url`. POST to the `callback_url` to mark the bug as fixed and re-enable the associated journey for future runs. Compatible with Linear, GitHub Issues, Jira, and any tracker that accepts HTTP webhooks.

## Who It's For

- **Developers building with AI** — Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, Lovable, Bolt, and similar tools. AI writes the code fast; Replay QA closes the QA gap.
- **Solo builders and small teams** — no QA headcount, no test suite. Replay QA is the only QA layer they need.
- **Software factories and AI coding platforms** — embed Replay QA as a quality gate via API so every generated app is tested before it ships.
- **Teams with existing CI** — already running Playwright or Cypress? Replay QA records every run and analyzes every failure.

## The Technology

Replay captures the full browser runtime at the Chromium level — not a video or a JavaScript shim. The recording is deterministic: the same session can be replayed and inspected retroactively, with the ability to add console logs and inspect state at any point in time without re-running the app. This makes AI root cause analysis accurate in ways that aren't possible from error logs or stack traces alone.

What Replay records per session:
- Render chains (which component re-rendered, what triggered it, what changed)
- State flow (Redux actions, React state updates, context changes)
- Network timing (every request and response with exact payload and timing)
- JS execution (every function call on every frame, with arguments and return values)
- DOM mutations (what changed in the DOM, when, and what code caused it)

## Pricing

- **Free**: 20 analyses per month. No credit card required.
- **Individual**: $49/month (or $42/month billed annually). 50 analyses per month.
- **Team**: $299/month (or ~$349/month billed monthly). 300 analyses per month.
- **Enterprise**: Custom. Includes API access for software factory integration.

## Company

Founded by ex-Mozilla engineers who spent a decade building the Firefox browser engine. Replay's recording technology is used by engineering teams at Vercel, Glide, Pantheon, Metabase, Tablecheck, and more. Endorsed by React maintainers Dan Abramov and Sebastian Markbåge.

Mission: Make the invisible visible — so every app ships with a QA layer, whether it's built by a solo developer, an AI agent, or a software factory.
